feeds.title: Sapiens Magazine
feeds.description: Sapiens, an editorially independent publication of the Wenner-Gren Foundation, is dedicated to popularizing anthropology to a broad audience. Sapiens aims to transform how the public understands anthropology. Every piece of content is grounded in anthropological research, theories, or thinking. We present stories and perspectives that are authoritative, accessible, and relevant - but still lively and entertaining.

feeds.title: Leiden Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: The Leiden Anthropology Blog is written by scholars at the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology of Leiden University. They blog about their research, teaching in the Bachelor and Master program, and share anthropological perspectives on a wide range of social issues.

feeds.title: The Geek Anthropologist
feeds.description: An anthropological approach to all things geek. A community blog where geek culture and its areas of interest are analysed through the perspective of sociocultural anthropology.

feeds.title: Engagement
feeds.description: A blog published by the Anthropology and Environment Society, a section of the American Anthropological Association Engagement blog publishes engaged scholarly research on anthro & environment issues.

feeds.title: FoodAnthropology
feeds.description: Wisdom from the Society for the Anthropology of Food and Nutrition.

feeds.title: Anthroholic
feeds.description: Explore the diversity of Human culture with Anthroholic Blog. Anthroholic is a platform dedicated to the fascinating discipline of Anthropology. Created by a team of passionate Anthropology enthusiasts who believe in the power of education, Anthroholic provides free, high-quality education in Anthropology to anyone interested.

feeds.title: The New York Times
feeds.description: News about archaeology and anthropology. Commentary and archival information about archaeology and anthropology from The New York Times.

feeds.title: Allegra
feeds.description: Allegra Lab is a publication platform, a collective of academics, and a movement. It is a small group of renegade anthropologists creating a voice for themselves in the margins of the neoliberal academy.

feeds.title: Somatosphere
feeds.description: Somatosphere is a collaborative website covering the intersections of medical anthropology, science and technology studies, cultural psychiatry, psychology, and bioethics. The goal for Somatosphere is not only to publish engaging essays, reviews, & new research in medical anthropology & social science but to incorporate the flexibility & networking capabilities of digital media, generating new & rich links in & among ideas & across disciplinary boundaries.

feeds.title: ScienceDaily
feeds.description: Anthropology news. Read about early human culture, civilizations and latest discoveries at ancient sites in our anthropology news.

feeds.title: Ethnography.com
feeds.description: A group blog on a variety of topics related to sociology, anthropology, and the human condition. We seek to change the way the world thinks about the Social Sciences in general, and Ethnography in particular.

feeds.title: Perspectives in Anthropology
feeds.description: Perspectives in Anthropology, is a new online publication series launched in 2014. The series specializes in articles in any field of Social Anthropology which are available online as open-access and free-to-read. All publications in the series are evaluated by an open-source, peer-review process.

feeds.title: Alma Gottlieb
feeds.description: Cultural anthropologist, researcher, author, and teacher impassioned by understanding all things human.

feeds.title: Platypus
feeds.description: From the Committee on the Anthropology of Science, Technology, and Computing.

feeds.title: Society for Medical Anthropology
feeds.description: (SMA), formed in 1967 and incorporated into the American Anthropological Association (AAA) in 1971, is dedicated to the profession and practice of medical anthropology, which uses concepts and methods from anthropology to produce new understandings of health, disease, illness, treatment, and care.

feeds.title: Teaching Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: Teaching Anthropology (TA) is a peer-reviewed, open-access journal dedicated to the teaching of anthropology. It is a journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute and promotes dialogue & reflection on anthropological pedagogies in schools, colleges, universities, & beyond. The journal brings together a range of formats & resources, from full-length peer-reviewed articles to shorter Developing Teaching reports.

feeds.title: Arctic Anthropology
feeds.description: This blog is run out of the anthropology research team at the Arctic Centre, University of Lapland, Finland. Here, you'll find the latest updates and news from Northern Anthropologies of Circumpolar Regions.

feeds.title: Anthropology For Beginners
feeds.description: The 'Anthropology for Beginners' blog by Suman Nath. This blog contains lots of study materials on Anthropology and related topics.

feeds.title: Anthroecologycom
feeds.description: Read the Anthro-Ecology blog and keep up with the latest updates.

feeds.title: Anthropology 365 Blog
feeds.description: I'm Adam Johnson, an anthropologist. The goal of this website is to provide space for me to apply anthropological thinking across the news, pop-culture, science, pop-science, film, music, video games, and anything else that catches my fancy.

feeds.title: Anthropology Department Blog
feeds.description: The National Association for the Practice of Anthropology was founded in 1983 to promote the practice of anthropology and the interests of practicing anthropologists, and to further the practice of anthropology as a profession.

feeds.title: Visual Anthropology of Japan
feeds.description: In the spirit of open-text, collaboration, communication and good anthropology… Visual Anthropology of Japan explores Japanese culture through photography, film and other visual methods.

feeds.title: Anthropolitan Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to Anthropolitan - UCL Anthropology's student-run blog. We publish blog posts, articles, stories, poems, and reviews relating to anthropology in all its diversity.

feeds.title: All Tomorrow's Cultures
feeds.description: Occasional posts on anthropologically interesting science fiction, anthropological futures and my own future as an anthropologist by Samuel Gerald Collins. samuel is a professor of anthropology at a mid-sized, state university in Maryland, USA.

feeds.title: Genetically Wrapped
feeds.description: Genetically Wrapped is a blog that focuses on humanity, our evolution, and society. Genetically Wrapped seeks to offer a thought-provoking, insightful and accessible understanding of the relationship between our genes, ourselves, and society.

feeds.title: anthropod
feeds.description: Anthropod is a blog documenting how a cultural anthropologist thinks about research, teaching, and the ways that we live in and shape the world around us. Anthropod is written by Lorena Gibson, an anthropologist and musician based in Wellington, Aotearoa New Zealand.

feeds.title: Anthropology.net
feeds.description: The website intends to promote and facilitate discussion, review research, extend stewardship of resources, and disseminate knowledge. Anthropology.net's mission is to create a cohesive online community of individuals interested in anthropology.

feeds.title: This Week In Pennsylvania Archaeology
feeds.description: The Section of Archaeology at The State Museum of Pennsylvania curates the largest collection in the museum and is responsible for multiple functions within the PHMC. Developing and maintaining exhibits in the Hall of Anthropology and Archaeology is a primary function, but our role as the state repository for cultural resource projects is substantial.

feeds.title: Andy White Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: Andrew White is an anthropological archaeologist with interests in hunter gatherers, lithic technology, human evolution, and complex systems theory. Andrew is interested in combining archaeological methods and theory with ethnographic data and computational modeling to develop new ways to push the boundaries of our understanding of the social, cultural, and evolutionary aspects of the human past.

feeds.title: UCL
feeds.description: This five-year project at UCL Anthropology employs a team of ten anthropologists who work on a collaborative & comparative project based on simultaneous 16-month ethnographies. This project investigates fundamental changes in people's relationship to age & health associated with the global rise of the smartphone. We will examine the impact on this ambivalence of smartphones and previously youth associated technologies.

feeds.title: Dienekes' Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: Dienekes' Anthropology blog is dedicated to human population genetics, physical anthropology, archaeology, and history.

feeds.title: Philbu's Blog
feeds.description: Anthropology of media and technology, Indigenous internet practices and media, technology enhanced learning and ethnographic fieldwork.

feeds.title: Anthropossibilities
feeds.description: A blog that captures the beauty of humanity and culture in order to understand the diversity and social existence of humans throughout history. Explore all the possibilities the world of Anthropology offers.

feeds.title: Anthropology Yesterday Blog
feeds.description: Anthropology Yesterday is a website created by me, Alex Golub, a professor of anthropology at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa. It's a place where I explore the history of anthropology in dribs and drabs at the pace of the old, pre-social media Internet.

feeds.title: Matt Artz
feeds.description: Matt Artz is an anthropologist, artist, and activist who advocates for the responsible design of human-centered technologies. He creates music and visual art.

feeds.title: anthro everywhere!
feeds.description: A collection of writings that speak to the anthropological perspective focusing on examples of public issues that we can better understand if we apply an anthropological lens, what anthropologists can bring to a workplace, and resources for teaching anthropology in and outside of the anthropology classroom and everywhere else.

feeds.title: The Rockstar Anthropologist
feeds.description: Myeashea Alexander is a physical anthropology grad student and science and art enthusiast. This blog is to de-mystify the world of Anthropology! This all-inclusive discipline needs better PR.

feeds.title: Sound Ethnography Project
feeds.description: The Sound Ethnography Project is an experiment in engaging with sound to produce novel ethnographic methods and forms. The project began out of the University of California, Irvine through the collaborative initiative of graduate students in anthropology.

feeds.title: Anthropologizing
feeds.description: Anthropologizing features a mixed-bag of posts on applied social research, business anthropology, design and user experience research, social observations, and other topics by Portland-based anthropologist and design researcher Amy L. Santee.

feeds.title: Violent metaphors
feeds.description: I study the genomes of modern and ancient peoples in order to uncover details of human prehistory. This is a blog about my passions: science, conflict, adventure, and interesting people.

feeds.title: Anthropological Tourism
feeds.description: This website was developed to provide a platform for sharing information about the impact of tourism on the people involved (the travelers, the destination managers, the hosts, the guests, the proprietors, the indigenous populations, the residents, and everyone else) from an anthropological perspective.

feeds.title: Cultural Heritage Anthropological Tourism Consultants
feeds.description: Welcome to Cultural Heritage Anthropological Tourism Consultants (CHATC) is a group of freelance ancient cultural heritage anthropological consultants from different countries with a base in Cape Verde, a turning point for cultural tourism in Africa, the Middle East and Asia respectively. Our services range from, cultural tours, organizers of cultural festivals, treks, travels, cultural exhibitions, antiques

feeds.title: Anthropology News
feeds.description: Anthropology News (AN) is the American Anthropological Association's news source. The American Anthropological Association is the world's largest association for professional anthropologists, with more than 10,000 members. Based in Washington, DC, the Association was founded in 1902, and covers all four main fields of anthropology.

feeds.title: Wenner-Gren Foundation
feeds.description: The Wenner-Gren Foundation for Anthropological Research, Inc. is a private operating foundation dedicated to the advancement of anthropology throughout the world.

feeds.title: Public Anthropologist
feeds.description: Public Anthropologist is an international peer-reviewed journal. This blog contains original posts, presentations of articles that will appear on the journal, conversations, and other relevant information.

feeds.title: John Hawks Blog
feeds.description: John Hawks is the Vilas-Borghesi Distinguished Achievement Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin Madison. John Hawks weblog on paleoanthropology, evolution and genetics is Tracking research into human origins, from the field to the laboratory.

feeds.title: anthro{dendum}
feeds.description: Anthro{dendum} is a group blog devoted to 'doing anthropology in public' — providing well-written relevant discussion of sociocultural anthropology that everyone will find accessible.

feeds.title: Zero Anthropology
feeds.description: This blog is primarily dedicated to sharing news, information, and opinions on topics dealing with globalism, globalization, liberalism, imperialism, working class politics, and the political economy of knowledge production in the social sciences and in anthropology specifically. Authored by Maximilian Forte, Professor, Political Anthropology.

feeds.title: Anthropological Spin
feeds.description: Pedal Powered Anthropology is an educational nonprofit dedicated to humanizing science, cultural exploration, and the humanities. Whether written, photographer, or on video, Anthrospin is connecting people to the rich cultural histories underlying sometimes everyday places and objects. Beyond that, Pedal Powered Anthropology teaches you how to look at things anthropologically.

feeds.title: Museum Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: Online Supplement to Museum Anthropology, the Journal of the Council for Museum Anthropology, a section of the American Anthropological Association

feeds.title: The Ethnobotanical Assembly
feeds.description: The Ethnobotanical Assembly (TEA) is a quarterly online magazine for research, writing, and thinking about people-plant relationships.

feeds.title: Living Anthropologically Blog
feeds.description: Living Anthropologically showcases anthropology's undying faith in the richness & variability of humankind. Let's bring anthropology to life & public debates.

feeds.title: Anthropology Daily
feeds.description: Anthropologydaily is dedicated to blogging all things cultural, physical, and archaeological.

feeds.title: Forensic Anthropology Blog
feeds.description: A Forensic Anthropology Blog by Chris on Tumblr.
